::: notes
Bridge from the bin: "The usual answer is another standard everyone has to follow. But as the saying goes: standards are like toothbrushes. Everybody wants one. Nobody wants to use anybody else's."

1:20.

Everyone sorts their bricks their own way, and nobody adopts someone else's system. So datom doesn't ask you to sort: it keeps the set.

Click: the title turns. "So datom keeps its own." Point at the box: the hashes, manifest, version log and parquet are datom's toothbrush. It stays in the box, and datom applies it. You only ever call `datom_write()` and `datom_read()`.

Every build records its exact pieces and its instructions, without anyone filing anything. It's what Lego does with its sets: any set since the 1950s has a number, an exact parts list and its instructions, so you can rebuild it today. datom does that for data.

The quote is often credited to Connie Morella (2006), but older versions exist; hence "as the saying goes".
:::
